editorial:
Imagine coming home from a year on the moon only to find that your life on Earth is a total mess. That is exactly what happens to Cassie, a NASA botanist who lands back on Earth just to realize she is completely disconnected from everyone she loves. She ends up at a quiet cabin in the woods to visit her twin sister, Stella. Stella used to work for NASA too, but she quit to start a new life with a climate activist named Bryan. The vibe is very quiet and tense, feeling more like a family fight than a space movie. You can really feel the awkwardness and the anger between the two sisters as they try to figure out if they can even be in the same room together.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the two leads do a great job showing how much they hurt each other without saying it out loud. The pace is slow, which might bore some of you, but it helps you feel the weight of their broken relationship. If you like stories about family secrets and second chances, you will love this. It looks beautiful, so you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the forest details. Or, if you like owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the sisters finally facing the truth about why they stopped talking. They realize that their rivalry was fueled by pressure from their parents and their jobs at NASA. After a big emotional blowout, they decide to stop competing and start supporting each other. The final scenes show them finding a small piece of peace together in the woods, proving that their bond as twins is stronger than their professional jealousy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about sibling relationships.
